musee-air-espace-le-bourget.name: Musée de l'Air et de l'Espace

rows.item: Soyuz T-6 descent module (Jean-Loup Chretien, Salyut 7, June-July 1982)
rows.notes: Museum collection page names the capsule and gives location as the Hall de l'Espace. Page did not state a display date.

rows.item: Soyuz TMA-03M descent module (Andre Kuipers, Dec 2011-Jul 2012)
rows.notes: Museum home page: 'take a look inside Andre Kuipers' original Soyuz capsule'. Wikipedia (Soyuz TMA-03M) says permanent display since 19 Sep 2016. Orrery entry 'Soyuz TMA' used as family match (TMA-03M is a TMA-M variant).

rows.item: Sokol suit worn by Andre Kuipers on Soyuz TMA-03M
rows.notes: Only Wikipedia says the suit is displayed alongside the capsule; museum pages I could read do not mention it. Suit model (KV-2) assumed from era, not verified.

rows.item: Ariane 1 engine block with four Viking 2 engines ('original engine part of Ariane I')
rows.notes: nl.wikipedia lists 'Motorblok van de Ariane I met vier Viking 2-motoren'; a Commons file caption says 'original engine part'. Whether it flew or is a test/spare unit is not stated. Commons also has a separate 'Viking rocket engine for Ariane 5' photo. Museum's own page not found.

rows.item: 'Old Vulcain engine' on display at the CSG museum
rows.notes: Only a 2004 photo caption. Vulcain 1 vs 2, flown vs test unit, and current display not verified.
Commons category title only; not confirmed that it is her flown suit, nor the suit model. Cité site unreachable (ECONNREFUSED).

rows.item: Mir engineering model with its original equipment
rows.notes: fr.wikipedia: 'modèle d'ingénierie de la station spatiale Mir'. Commons labels it 'Model of Mir'. Real ground engineering model vs mock-up not established.
